import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.metrics import log_loss
import os

# Set seed for reproducibility
np.random.seed(42)

# Load data
train = pd.read_csv("./input/train.csv")
test = pd.read_csv("./input/test.csv")

# Get feature columns (exclude id and species)
feature_cols = [col for col in train.columns if col not in ["id", "species"]]

# Extract features
X_train = train[feature_cols].values
y_train = train["species"].values
X_test = test[feature_cols].values

# Create hold-out validation split (30% validation to ensure we train on only training data)
X_train_split, X_val, y_train_split, y_val = train_test_split(
    X_train, y_train, test_size=0.2, random_state=42, stratify=y_train
)

# Train Random Forest model
model = RandomForestClassifier(
    n_estimators=200, max_depth=30, n_jobs=-1, random_state=42
)
model.fit(X_train_split, y_train_split)

# Validate predictions and compute logloss on hold-out set
val_predictions = model.predict_proba(X_val)
val_logloss = log_loss(y_val, val_predictions)
print(f"Hold-out Validation LogLoss: {val_logloss:.6f}")

# Make predictions on test set
test_predictions = model.predict_proba(X_test)

# Prepare submission file matching sample_submission format
species_cols = train["species"].unique()
submission = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "id": test["id"],
        **{col: test_predictions[i] for i, col in enumerate(sorted(species_cols))},
    }
)

# Ensure probabilities are in valid range [0, 1]
submission = submission.apply(lambda x: x.clip(0, 1))

# Save to submission directory
submission.to_csv("./submission/submission.csv", index=False)
print(f"Submission saved to ./submission/submission.csv")
print(f"Submission shape: {submission.shape}")
